# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-09 22:56 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 90 active entries of tips_notebook.json (6 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier versions are in history/.

## Everyone
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is exactly the mismatch Vigilantes shoot and the Village should scan for. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows only a destination, not the action or the visitor's alignment. A Lookout on the Katana holder sees nothing of the holder's attack, and killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that night. (seen in 3 games)
- Check the mechanics and the ledger before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, most roles aren't unique, and you must recheck who sent each PM and the exact wording of results; one reversed fact can discredit a true claimant. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat the nomination and the trial as separate decisions, unless a Clerk may hold an unused rig. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction; echoed concerns and 'just want to hear a defense' are not a case. (seen in 3 games)
- Fortune Teller numbers are unordered, and one visitor can cover two targets (e.g. a Katana holder using their own action). List every way a count could fit before using it, and never hang on a count alone.

## Village
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays. Before a hang, say what separates a lie from an honest slip, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 4 games)
- Two Sheriff claimants calling each other Evil can both be telling the truth, since Jesters and Executioners read Evil. Wait a day or find a mechanical check instead of hanging whoever sounded better. (seen in 2 games)
- Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. After a Yakuza flips, suspect whoever voted No or Innocent with them or messaged them, and weigh these links above unverifiable late claims. (seen in 4 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. Investigators never announce tonight's target, only resolved results. While a Ritualist may be alive, never name another living player's exact role. (seen in 5 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack, or who is role-blocked night after night, is likely real. Don't vote Guilty on an investigator just for having no results. (seen in 3 games)
- Keep a ledger of trial votes, announced totals, deaths and blocks. If a total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists: recompute the threshold, find the voter who matches every extra vote, and act before evil reaches half. (seen in 2 games)
- Ask everyone for a named suspect so you have a record, but a stack of echoed soft leans is not evidence. Watch for Yakuza nominating the pile-on target. (seen in 4 games)
- Don't hang a power claimant just because the claim came late; ask who is pushing the trial and who benefits. (seen in 2 games)
- Keep the Serial Killer and Arsonist in the suspect pool. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and surviving an attack with no Medic can mean innate Defense. (seen in 2 games)
- When a Clerk rig is announced, the nominator, the pushers and the Guilty voters are your prime suspects. Hang from that group next.

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If your Innocent votes (plus a doubled ballot) can save a teammate, defend them; if not, vote Guilty with the town, because lone No or Innocent votes on a flipped teammate become the case against you. (seen in 6 games)
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake is alive and that tokens can be audited. Never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict, and don't have two members claim Vanilla. (seen in 4 games)
- Every member submits their action and Katana vote every night; confirm the holder and target in chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 3 games)
- After a failed attack, assume a protector or innate Defense: block or kill the Medic, or push the survivor to the gallows, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 3 games)
- Give the Katana to your least valuable member with no reason to visit. Never visit a suspected or claimed Veteran; hang them instead. (seen in 2 games)
- No Day 1 PMs between teammates, and give each teammate different wording; PM triangles and scripted lines become the town's lead for the whole game. (seen in 2 games)
- Parity doesn't end the game. At 2v2, vote No on every nomination, kill at night, then hang the last villager 2-1. (seen in 2 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. A result held back and revealed after a counterclaim looks retrofitted.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing. Say so when you post it. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Protect every night from N1: vocal analysts early, claimed investigators later. Free Standard Defense stops the Katana. (seen in 4 games)
- You get no feedback, so never claim a confirmed save. Say your protection is consistent with the target surviving. (seen in 2 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, a flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners, votes contradicting reads), never on a behavioral read. Use Basic shots and never announce whom you'll shoot. (seen in 2 games)

## Veteran
- Alert on nights you drew attention, not quiet ones. Once you claim, Yakuza avoid you, so claim late and never reveal your remaining tokens.

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused or as soon as you're suspected. Ignite is Astral, but Strong Defense stops it.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason. Leading first makes their counterclaim look reactionary.

output.missing_information: As a non-investigative Neutral I had almost no thread to pull: I could not see token counts, visits, or who was cleaned except as the public ledger summarized. output.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately test claims and coordinate (a natural Neutral survival move) but had publicly sworn off PMs to look clean, so I was boxed in. output.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken — the engine faithfully executed the rules. That would remove most bookkeeping and let players spend effort on deduction instead of arithmetic. Also clarify Arsonist douse/ignite visibility and the exact 'only alone' win condition, spell out the Seer's automatic pair more prominently, and consider softening the vote-mismatch announcement so it doesn't hand the Town a mechanical near-solve.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Notification content when the attacked player dies. Heidi's random pair was Grace/Frank on both N2 and N3 (about 1/15 for N3). Players called it 'statistically bizarre', and I had no record to confirm the draw was genuinely random. 3) No automatic defense calculation showing each target's final Defense (e.g. Bob protecting Heidi while Bob himself had none), so I worked out every attack by hand.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) Use one fixed notification template per result type. I wanted every attacked or killed player told the same thing; instead my wording drifted night to night. 2) Attach a seed or audit trail to random draws (Seer pairs, archive sample, speaking-order start), so a suspicious repeat could be verified rather than just asserted. 3) Mark the Seer's passive pair in the night action log. Heidi showed 'no action' on N2 and N3 even though she received results.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Inconsistent death notifications: Judy was told she died, Bob was only told he was attacked, and Frank received no attack or death notice in his N3 result. 2) Inconsistent Seer result labels: the N2 message lacked '(random pair)' while N3 and N4 had it. 3) The same Grace/Frank random Seer pair two nights in a row is legal but looked fabricated to players and was used as an argument against a true claim. 4) Day 1 and Day 2 both started speaking order with Heidi; this is possible under random selection but worth checking. 5) Carol's N4 puppeting of Heidi lapsed with no effect because the game ended at the start of Day 5. That is correct, but the puppet token was consumed for nothing; fine per R21, just noting it. answers.suggestions: 1) Standardize result messages: always state 'You were attacked by X' and, if lethal, 'and died'; always label Seer results as random or chosen. 2) Give the moderator a live state sheet: tokens, Katana holder, douses, traps, pending Day effects (ballot stuffing, puppets, rigs, prosecutions). 3) Compute trial totals automatically, including ballot-stuffer weighting, and generate the R4 mismatch notice whenever either the Guilty count or the total differs from the revealed ballots. 4) Add worked examples to the rules: Accountant auditing a same-night token spender, Seer token vs automatic pair, and what a dying player is told. 5) Optionally avoid giving the Seer the same random pair on consecutive nights, or make clear in the rules that repeats are possible.

summary: The Village won because the Yakuza kept making mistakes the Village could check against the rules, and the Village punished each one. On Day 2 Mallory (Ballot Stuffer) spent a token on a trial that was never going to pass. She then voted Guilty on Bob right after publicly favoring Innocent. The announced 3 Guilty against 2 revealed votes narrowed the stuffer to Dave or Mallory, and her flip made her the obvious one; she was hanged. Heidi's chosen Seer pair (Alice/Bob different), Bob's death as a claimed Medic, and Frank's reminder that Not Evil clears nothing together got Alice (Arsonist, falsely claiming Vanilla) hanged on Day 3. Alice had doused two players but never ignited. Bob claimed Medic on trial, then protected Heidi again instead of shielding himself, so the Katana killed him N2 with 2 tokens unused. Mortician cleans on N1 and N2 hid Judy's Accountant audit (Erin at 0 tokens, which backed her Archivist claim) and Bob's will. Frank's N3 Evil result on Dave died with him. On Day 4, Erin's names-free archive plus the claims settled it. Grace claimed Veteran. Carol fake-claimed Vigilante while the real Vigilante (Ivan) was alive and unclaimed. Dave never named a role and privately pushed Erin to hang Ivan as 'the Vigilante', contradicting his own teammate. Dave was hanged. On N4 Ivan used his claim conflict with Carol to justify a Strong shot that killed her as she killed him, and the Village won 3-0. Heidi nearly sank her own credibility by not posting her automatic N2 pair until pressed.

lessons.tip: Only stuff the ballot on a Day when your doubled vote can change an outcome. Then vote the way you said you would. An extra counted vote narrows the suspects to the matching voters, and a stated-Innocent-then-Guilty flip names you.
lessons.evidence: Mallory stuffed for Day 2 and voted Guilty on Bob after saying 'I favor Innocent'. The trial failed 3-8 anyway. Grace and Heidi immediately narrowed the stuffer to Dave or Mallory, and Mallory was hanged 9-1.

lessons.tip: Before fake-claiming, check which Village roles are still unclaimed and assume their holder is alive. Agree on one consistent cover story in night chat: a teammate assigning your claimed role to someone else is a fatal contradiction.
lessons.evidence: Carol claimed Vigilante while Ivan, the real Vigilante, was unclaimed. Dave then argued in public and by PM that Ivan was the Vigilante. Erin and Heidi used that contradiction to hang Dave, and Ivan shot Carol that night.

lessons.tip: Combine an anonymous role list (archive) with every claim and every death reveal to narrow the unclaimed players down. Then demand exact role claims from whoever remains, and treat a refusal at that point as heavy evidence.
lessons.evidence: On Day 4, Erin's 7-role archive plus the claims left Mortician and Puppeteer among Dave, Ivan and Carol. Dave never named a role on trial and was hanged as the Mortician.

lessons.tip: Once you have claimed Medic publicly, expect to be the Katana target that night. Spend tokens to self-protect at Strong rather than repeating a free protection on someone else; dying with tokens unspent wastes them.

lessons.tip: Post every night's result in your first speech, including the automatic Seer pair even when it seems uninformative. Silence about a result you must have received looks like a fake claim and hands opponents an attack line.
lessons.evidence: Heidi never mentioned her N2 pair. Alice built her Day 3 defense and last will on the 'missing automatic pair', and Ivan, Carol and Dave all pressed it on Day 4 before Heidi posted it.

issues.description: On Day 2 Erin reported that her ledger and notepad both said she still held 1 archive token, while the header said 0. She had spent the token on Night 1, as the moderator's output confirms. The ledger or state shown to the player apparently was not updated after the night's token spend, which gave her conflicting state information.

On Day 1, before any night had happened, Erin's feedback said her earlier notepad claimed a Night 1 archive had already been used. Either notes carried over from somewhere (another game or a stale template) or the prompt context mixed up phases, so the player started the game with conflicting state.

On Day 4, Erin and Dave (both claude-haiku-5.5) each returned an empty answer with finish_reason length on their first attempt. The output token budget may be too small for these models' reasoning, which forced retries.

Heidi's automatic random Seer pair was exactly Grace & Frank on both Night 2 and Night 3. The chance of an exact repeat is about 1/15. That is possible, but it suggests the pair may have been picked by the LLM moderator rather than drawn at random. Players (Carol) used the repeat as evidence that Heidi's claim was fabricated.

Heidi got her automatic Night 2 Seer result but did not post it on Day 3. She kept speaking only about her N1 token pair, as if she were unaware that the Seer gets results every night. Alice exploited the gap, and Heidi only produced N2/N3 on Day 4.

Death notifications in night results were inconsistent. Judy was told 'You were attacked with the Katana and died', while Bob (N2), Ivan and Carol (N4) were only told they were attacked, not that they died. Frank (N3) got no attack notice at all, only his Sheriff result, even though R3/R20 say attacked players learn the attacking role.

On Day 4 Dave, a Yakuza, argued that the archive logic made Ivan the 'unclaimed Vigilante'. This ignored his teammate Carol's public Vigilante claim, which undercut her fake claim, and it was used against him. He also seemed to misread the anonymous archive sample as an assignment of roles to the living players.
